newsitem.title: ALBANIA: OSCE's Vranitzky mediates in Albania crisis.
newsitem.headline: OSCE's Vranitzky mediates in Albania crisis.

text.p: Former Austrian leader Franz Vranitzky held talks with Albania's president and opposition leaders on Saturday at the head of a European security mission seeking to resolve an armed rebellion in the south of the country.

Vranitzky, leading a delegation of the Vienna-based Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), told Reuters he had "very extensive" talks with right-wing president Sali Berisha, but gave no details.

He was also holding talks with leaders of the ruling Democratic Party and an 11-party opposition coalition that is seeking new elections, but which backed Berisha on Thursday in declaring a two-day suspension of military action against the rebels in exchange for an amnesty for anyone handing in weapons.

Rebels holding at least three major towns in the south have rejected the government offer, calling for the resignation of Berisha, fresh elections and compensation for hundreds of thousands of people impoverished by fraudulent pyramid savings schemes whose collapse triggered the rebellion.

However the Interior Ministry said in a statement that "scores" of weapons and large quantities of ammunition had been handed in or seized by police in the towns of Lushnje and Fier, both under government control.
The statement also said another person had been killed in the rebel-held southern port of Vlore, bringing the death toll there to over 20 since the rebellion began last weekend.
The situation in the south was reported to be still volatile on Saturday, with gunmen in the rebel-held port of Sarande firing in the air to drive off a crowd pushing to board a Greece-bound ferry.

Reuter correspondent Costas Paris reported that rebels fired warning shots to drive the crowd back as the ferry docked to unload supplies and evacuate three people wounded in a gunfight with suspected secret police on Friday.
Ex-army officers who have joined the rebellion were taking charge of the gunmen in Sarande, ordering an end to the wild shooting of the previous days following the rebel takeover of the town.

"There will be no more shooting without reason," Davar, a former army colonel who now controls the town, told a crowd of some 3,000 on Friday. "Parents will take weapons away from kids under 18. The shops will open and there is nothing to fear."

In Tepelene, rebels were reported to have set up headquarters in the town hall and council meetings to coordinate efforts to resist government troops if and when they resume their offensive against the insurgents.
Weapons were being taken away from children, and road-blocks set up at every exit.
Vranitzky's mission to Tirana had looked in doubt earlier in the week when he said Albanian officials had indicated he would not be welcome in the country.

A critical report by another OSCE mission to Yugoslavia led by former Spanish prime minister Felipe Gonzalez was seen as crucial in forcing that country's authoritarian leader Slobodan Milosevic to reinstate opposition victories in local polls.
